summary.en: Choose lists, sets and maps by their ordering, uniqueness and lookup contracts.
summary.bn: ডেটার ক্রম, একই মান রাখা আর খোঁজার ধরন বুঝে লিস্ট, সেট বা ম্যাপ বেছে নাও।

notes: All programs use Java 17 APIs and language rules.

sections.title: Choose a container from the question you ask
Declare the behaviour and choose an implementation
Read entries without accidental structural changes
Match the collection to a small use case
Protect key identity and state assumptions
Collections used here work on Java 17
Make collection behaviour part of the design

examples.title: Contrast a list and an endpoint queue
examples.explanationHtml: Value removal leaves the later duplicate in place. LinkedList removes A from the front.

examples.title: Keep unique rolls and display them sorted
examples.explanationHtml: The hash set handles uniqueness. A tree set gives a predictable increasing display.

examples.title: Count words and order the keys
examples.explanationHtml: Each repeated word updates its existing map entry. Sorting is applied explicitly before printing.

practice.title: Unique roll numbers
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..30) then n roll numbers (1..999). Print a TreeSet-style bracketed ascending sequence with duplicates removed. No prompt.

practice.title: Sorted word frequencies
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..30) then n lowercase ASCII word tokens. Print word count on separate lines in lexical order, or EMPTY for n=0. No prompt.
hints: Increment a map value using getOrDefault.

practice.title: Pick a marks container
practice.statementHtml: A lecturer repeatedly reads marks by position and appends new marks. Compare ArrayList with LinkedList.
practice.answerHtml: ArrayList supports constant-time indexed reads and amortized constant-time append. LinkedList requires walking nodes for an index and uses extra link storage. Choose ArrayList for this access pattern.

practice.title: Repair mutable map keys
practice.statementHtml: A student key uses a mutable roll number in equals and hashCode. The roll changes after insertion. Explain a safe redesign.
practice.answerHtml: Make roll identity immutable and use a separate editable profile for other details. Alternatively, remove a key before changing identity and reinsert it. Do not mutate hash identity inside the map.
hints: Lookup uses the stored hashing arrangement.

quiz.prompt: Which occurrence is removed by remove(Integer.valueOf(70))?
quiz.explanation: The value overload removes the first equal element; the queue removes its first arrival.

quiz.prompt: How do uniqueness and sorted display affect the roll numbers?
quiz.explanation: HashSet keeps two values, and TreeSet prints them in natural order.

quiz.prompt: What sorted frequency lines result from the repeated word?
quiz.explanation: The map increments book twice and the TreeMap view sorts its keys.

quiz.prompt: Which interface associates roll numbers with marks?
quiz.explanation: A map uses keys for lookup and stores one value for each key.

quiz.prompt: Which operation is normally costly on an ArrayList?
Why can repeated LinkedList.get(i) traversal be quadratic?
options: Each indexed lookup may walk nodes
quiz.explanation: Indexed access is linear, so an indexed traversal repeats that work.

quiz.prompt: What ordering does HashMap promise for iteration?
quiz.explanation: Use a suitable ordered implementation when output order matters.

quiz.prompt: What does zero from a TreeSet comparator mean?
options: The elements are equivalent for set membership
The elements have equal memory addresses
quiz.explanation: TreeSet uses its ordering relation to identify duplicates.

quiz.prompt: Which removal fits a condition during list processing?
quiz.explanation: removeIf performs coordinated removal rather than invalidating an active enhanced-for traversal.

quiz.prompt: What must stay stable for a hash key while stored?
options: Fields involved in equals and hashCode
quiz.explanation: Changing identity-related state can make lookup search the wrong bucket.

keyPoints.en: List preserves positions and permits duplicates.
keyPoints.bn: লিস্টে পজিশন থাকে আর একই মান একাধিকবার রাখা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Set stores one representative per equivalent value.
keyPoints.bn: সেটে একই মান বারবার যোগ করলেও একবারই থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Map connects unique keys to values.
keyPoints.bn: ম্যাপ প্রতিটি আলাদা key-এর সঙ্গে একটি value রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Hash iteration order is not a sorting contract.
keyPoints.bn: হ্যাশ কালেকশনের প্রিন্ট করা ক্রম দেখে সাজানো ধরে নিও না।

keyPoints.en: Stable key identity keeps lookup reliable.
keyPoints.bn: key-এর পরিচয় বদলে না গেলে খুঁজে পাওয়া নির্ভরযোগ্য থাকে।

examQuestions.question: Compare ArrayList, LinkedList and TreeSet for a student register.
examQuestions.answerHtml: ArrayList supports indexed order and duplicates. LinkedList suits endpoint changes but has linear indexed access. TreeSet stores unique students in comparison order, so define a comparison consistent with the intended identity.

examQuestions.question: Why does putting an existing map key not increase size?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Each key identifies one mapping. A new put for an equal key replaces the value, while the key count stays unchanged.

examQuestions.question: Explain a safe way to print HashSet values in sorted order.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Construct a TreeSet from the set or sort a copied list. Print that ordered result rather than relying on hash iteration.
